summary: Validated iter_21 push-device management + pending-approval ding sound. Backend: 14/14 NEW tests + 28/28 regression PASS (42/42 total). New endpoints GET /api/push/devices and DELETE /api/push/devices/{id} verified end-to-end including subscribe→list→upsert-stability→404→delete→decrement→404-after-delete + unauth-rejection. _device_label_from_ua() helper unit-tested for iPhone/Safari, Android/Chrome, Windows/Chrome, Mac/Safari, Edge, empty, unknown — all PASS. POST /api/push/subscribe correctly stores user_agent + last_seen_at; $setOnInsert preserves id and created_at on repeated upserts. Frontend code review: all data-testids present in Notifications.jsx (devices-section, devices-list-count, device-row-{id}, device-delete-{id}, ding-test), removeDevice() handler correct (confirm dialog + DELETE call + local pushManager.unsubscribe when current endpoint matches), AdminDashboard imports installPendingApprovalDingListener and invokes it in useEffect, sw.js v53 BADGE_CHANGED postMessage includes require_approval + kind fields, notify-sound.js listener calls playPendingApprovalDing only when require_approval=true. Frontend live render of /admin/notifications crashed Playwright (Target crashed) — same memory issue reported in iter_20; tried 3 different approaches (set localStorage + navigate, smaller viewport, direct goto). NOT a product bug — Playwright headless browser pool runs out of memory loading the heavy admin dashboard route. Backend API path confirmed working from inside same browser context via fetch (GET /api/push/devices → 200 with 10 devices, all fields including label correctly populated).
action_items: (Optional) Investigate why /admin/notifications crashes the Playwright headless tab — likely AdminDashboard.jsx mounts too many widgets/eager-loads heavy bundles. Real browsers handle it fine (user has 10 active devices subscribed). Could split AdminDashboard into lazier route-level chunks.
critical_code_review_comments: _device_label_from_ua() in server.py (~line 5613): ordering of browser checks is correct — Edge before Chrome before Safari, since Chrome/Edge UAs both contain 'safari/'. Good defensive design.
DELETE /api/push/devices/{device_id} accepts either the id field OR the last-32-char suffix of endpoint (backward compat for legacy records without an id). Clean fallback.

POST /api/push/subscribe uses $setOnInsert for {id, created_at} so re-subscribes never regenerate the id — verified by test_03_resubscribe_same_endpoint_upserts_keeps_id_and_created_at. This is the correct upsert pattern.

Notifications.jsx removeDevice() correctly handles the 'current device' case: after backend DELETE it also calls pushManager.getSubscription().unsubscribe() and resets subscribed=false + currentEndpoint=''. No state-leak.
notify-sound.js uses anti-spam (800ms minimum between plays) which prevents an avalanche of pushes from cacophony — well thought through.
Service worker sw.js v53 only sets requireInteraction=true when kind==='overdue' OR require_approval is truthy — keeps regular notifications dismissible while pending approvals stick. Correct UX.

Minor: backend.out.log is now ~24MB. The historical 'Could not deserialize key data' lines are still STALE (pre-VAPID-fix), not from current pushes. Consider periodic log rotation (separate from this task).

rca of the issue: No bug found. Both feature requests (a) distinctive ding-ding sound via WebAudio 2-tone bell E6→G6 with 180ms gap, and (b) device management UI with delete capability, are correctly implemented end-to-end. Backend endpoints respond correctly, helper UA→label translation works for all common UAs, upsert semantics preserve id/created_at, frontend wiring (testids + handlers + SW message routing) is fully in place. The headless-browser crash during /admin/notifications render is a TEST infrastructure limitation (memory), not a product defect — the same admin route renders fine in real browsers per iter_20 evidence (user has 10 active subscribed devices showing real push delivery /api/push/test → sent=11/failed=0).
